entries.title: Scanlation
entries.subtitle: The act of scanning, translating, and editing unlicensed manga/manhwa for online distribution. A combination of "scan" + "translation".

payload.definition: The act of scanning, translating, and editing unlicensed manga/manhwa for online distribution. A combination of "scan" + "translation".

entries.title: Raw
entries.subtitle: The original, unedited image, usually in Japanese/Korean/Chinese. Can be a physical scan or a digital rip.

payload.definition: The original, unedited image, usually in Japanese/Korean/Chinese. Can be a physical scan or a digital rip.

entries.title: Chapter

payload.definition: An individual unit of manga publication, usually 15-25 pages for manga and 40-80+ panels for a webtoon.

entries.title: Tankoubon
entries.subtitle: A bound manga volume, usually containing 8-12 chapters. Tankoubon raws are higher quality than magazine raws.

payload.definition: A bound manga volume, usually containing 8-12 chapters. Tankoubon raws are higher quality than magazine raws.

entries.title: Webtoon

payload.definition: A Korean digital manhwa format, published as long vertical strips optimized for reading on mobile.

entries.title: Typesetting (TS)
entries.subtitle: The process of applying translated text to manga speech bubbles and text areas, including font choice, size, and positioning.

payload.definition: The process of applying translated text to manga speech bubbles and text areas, including font choice, size, and positioning.

entries.title: SFX
entries.subtitle: Sound Effects — onomatopoeia in manga (ドン, バン, etc.). Can be translated with an overlay or kept with a footnote.

payload.definition: Sound Effects — onomatopoeia in manga (ドン, バン, etc.). Can be translated with an overlay or kept with a footnote.

entries.title: Speech Bubble
entries.subtitle: The bounded area where dialogue text is placed. Types: speech, thought, narration, shout, whisper.

payload.definition: The bounded area where dialogue text is placed. Types: speech, thought, narration, shout, whisper.

entries.title: Kerning
entries.subtitle: Adjusting the spacing between pairs of characters to improve the visual appearance of text.

payload.definition: Adjusting the spacing between pairs of characters to improve the visual appearance of text.

entries.title: Leading
entries.subtitle: Vertical spacing between lines of text. Also called "line-height" or "line spacing".

payload.definition: Vertical spacing between lines of text. Also called "line-height" or "line spacing".

entries.title: Cleaning (CL)
entries.subtitle: The process of removing the original text and scan artifacts, and preparing the image to receive translated text.

payload.definition: The process of removing the original text and scan artifacts, and preparing the image to receive translated text.

entries.title: Redraw (RD)
entries.subtitle: Manually redrawing parts of the image that were damaged by text removal, especially over detailed illustrations.

payload.definition: Manually redrawing parts of the image that were damaged by text removal, especially over detailed illustrations.

entries.title: Inpainting
entries.subtitle: An AI technique that reconstructs removed areas of an image, filling them with plausible content based on the surrounding context.

payload.definition: An AI technique that reconstructs removed areas of an image, filling them with plausible content based on the surrounding context.

entries.title: Leveling
entries.subtitle: Adjusting white/black levels to improve image contrast and cleanliness. Essential for physical scan raws.

payload.definition: Adjusting white/black levels to improve image contrast and cleanliness. Essential for physical scan raws.

entries.title: Denoising
entries.subtitle: Removing noise/grain from an image, common in low-quality scans or photos of pages.

payload.definition: Removing noise/grain from an image, common in low-quality scans or photos of pages.

entries.title: Localization
entries.subtitle: Adapting a translation for the local audience, including idioms, cultural references, and jokes. Goes beyond literal translation.

payload.definition: Adapting a translation for the local audience, including idioms, cultural references, and jokes. Goes beyond literal translation.

entries.title: Honorifics
entries.subtitle: Japanese suffixes such as -san, -kun, -chan, -sama. A constant community debate over whether to keep or adapt them.

payload.definition: Japanese suffixes such as -san, -kun, -chan, -sama. A constant community debate over whether to keep or adapt them.

entries.title: T/N

payload.definition: Translator's Note — a note from the translator explaining cultural references, untranslatable puns, or necessary context.

payload.definition: Machine Translation — automated translation by machine (Google Translate, DeepL, etc.). Used as a base that requires human review.
